Consider the correct statements with regards to the Sultan of Johor Cup 2025:
1. The Sultan of Johor Cup is related to football.
2. India won a silver medal in this match.
3. Its first edition was held in 2011 in Malaysia.
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Sultan of Johor Cup is an annual invitational under-21 men's HOCKEY tournament, not football. Statement 2 is correct: India finished runners-up (silver) in the 2025 edition, losing the final 1-2 to Australia in Johor Bahru, with Anmol Ekka scoring India's goal. Statement 3 is correct: the tournament was established in 2011 and is held at the Taman Daya Hockey Stadium in Johor Bahru, Malaysia. Hence statements 2 and 3 only are correct. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Verified via Olympics.com and Hockey India match reports for the 2025 final.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Types of Reactions: Combination, Decomposition, Displacement
stem:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer:

| List I (Type of reaction) | List II (Equation) |
|---|---|
| A. Combination | 1. \(2\text{AgCl} \rightarrow 2\text{Ag} + \text{Cl}_2\) |
| B. Decomposition | 2. \(\text{CaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\) |
| C. Displacement | 3. \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{BaCl}_2 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4 + 2\text{NaCl}\) |
| D. Double Displacement | 4. \(\text{Fe} + \text{CuSO}_4 \rightarrow \text{FeSO}_4 + \text{Cu}\) |
solution: Combination joins two reactants into one product: \(\text{CaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\), so A-2. Decomposition splits one reactant into two: \(2\text{AgCl} \rightarrow 2\text{Ag} + \text{Cl}_2\), so B-1. Displacement has a more reactive element replacing another: \(\text{Fe} + \text{CuSO}_4 \rightarrow \text{FeSO}_4 + \text{Cu}\), so C-4. Double displacement exchanges ions between two compounds: \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{BaCl}_2 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4 + 2\text{NaCl}\), so D-3. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Redox: Oxidation, Reduction and Reducing Agents
stem:
Consider the following statements about the reaction: \(2\text{PbO(s)} + \text{C(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{Pb(s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}\).

1. Lead is getting reduced.
2. Carbon dioxide is getting oxidised.
3. Carbon is getting oxidised.
4. Lead oxide is getting reduced.

Which statements are incorrect?
solution: In \(2\text{PbO} + \text{C} \rightarrow 2\text{Pb} + \text{CO}_2\), lead oxide loses oxygen, so lead oxide is the species being reduced (statement 4 is correct), and carbon gains oxygen, so carbon is oxidised (statement 3 is correct). Statement 1 is incorrect because it is lead oxide, not lead, that is reduced; lead is the free metal produced. Statement 2 is incorrect because carbon dioxide is the product of the oxidation of carbon and is not itself being oxidised. Hence the incorrect statements are 1 and 2. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: On heating Lead Nitrate powder in a boiling tube, brown fumes are emitted. These fumes are of:
solution: Lead nitrate decomposes on heating as \(2\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{PbO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2\). The brown fumes are nitrogen dioxide, \(\text{NO}_2\). Oxygen is a colourless gas, lead oxide is the yellow solid residue left behind, and no nitric acid is formed in this dry thermal decomposition. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Consider the following reaction: \(\text{CaO(s)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}\)

1. A combination reaction.
2. An exothermic reaction.
3. An endothermic reaction.

Select the correct option:
solution: In \(\text{CaO(s)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}\) two reactants combine to give a single product, so it is a combination reaction and statement 1 is correct. Slaking of quick lime releases a large amount of heat, so the reaction is exothermic and statement 2 is correct, which automatically makes statement 3 wrong. Hence only 1 and 2 hold. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Types of Reactions: Combination, Decomposition, Displacement
stem: Which of the following is the correct balanced equation for the reaction of iron with steam?
solution: Iron reacts with steam to give magnetic iron oxide and hydrogen: \(3\text{Fe} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4 + 4\text{H}_2\). Atom check: Fe 3 on each side, O 4 on each side, H 8 on each side, so it is balanced and the product is correct. Option a is unbalanced and gives \(\text{FeO}\), option c gives \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\), which is not the steam product, and option d invents the non-existent \(\text{FeO}_2\). Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Consider the following observations that may occur during a process:

1. Evolution of a gas.
2. Change in state.
3. Change in temperature.
4. Change in colour.

Which of the above observations can help determine whether a chemical reaction has taken place?
solution: A chemical reaction is recognised by observable changes accompanying it: change in state, change in colour, evolution of a gas and change in temperature. All four of the listed observations are standard indicators of a chemical reaction. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Consider the following observations regarding corrosion:

I. Iron articles get coated with a reddish-brown powder.
II. Silver articles develop a green coating.
III. Copper develops a black coating.

Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?
solution: Statement I is correct: iron rusts to a reddish-brown powder of hydrated iron(III) oxide. Statement II is incorrect: silver tarnishes to a black coating of silver sulphide, \(\text{Ag}_2\text{S}\), not a green one. Statement III is incorrect: copper develops a green coating of basic copper carbonate, \(\text{CuCO}_3 \cdot \text{Cu(OH)}_2\), not a black one. So the incorrect statements are II and III. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Redox: Oxidation, Reduction and Reducing Agents
stem:
Regarding the reaction: \(\text{CuO} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{Cu} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)

Which statements are correct?

1. \(\text{CuO}\) is being reduced
2. \(\text{H}_2\) is being oxidised
3. This is a redox reaction.
solution: In \(\text{CuO} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{Cu} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\), copper oxide loses oxygen, so \(\text{CuO}\) is reduced and statement 1 is correct. Hydrogen gains oxygen to become water, so \(\text{H}_2\) is oxidised and statement 2 is correct. Since oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously in the same reaction, it is a redox reaction and statement 3 is correct. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Consider the following statements:

1. Calcium hydroxide reacts with carbon dioxide to form calcium carbonate and water.
2. It is an exothermic reaction.

Correct statement is:
solution: Statement 1 is correct: \(\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\) is the standard lime-water reaction that also gives the white precipitate test for carbon dioxide. Statement 2 is also correct: this carbonation reaction gives out heat. Using standard enthalpies of formation, \(\Delta H\) is about \(-113\) kJ per mole, so it is exothermic. Both statements are therefore correct. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Statement 2 (exothermic) is not stated verbatim in NCERT; keyed from standard enthalpies of formation, which give about -113 kJ/mol for the carbonation of slaked lime. Low-confidence only in the sense that a setter treating the thermicity as untaught might have intended 'A'.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Consider the following reaction: \(\text{FeSO}_4\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\text{(s)} + \text{SO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{SO}_3\text{(g)}\)

1. Ferrous sulphate is green in colour and it gets reduced to ferric oxide.
2. Evolution of Sulphur dioxide gas can be confirmed by a moist blue litmus paper by bringing it to the mouth of the test tube.
3. The reaction gives an enormous amount of heat.

Incorrect code:
solution: The balanced thermal decomposition is \(2\text{FeSO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{SO}_2 + \text{SO}_3\). Statement 1 is incorrect: ferrous sulphate crystals are indeed green, but iron goes from \(+2\) in \(\text{FeSO}_4\) to \(+3\) in \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\), which is oxidation, not reduction. Statement 2 is correct: \(\text{SO}_2\) is an acidic oxide and turns moist blue litmus paper red. Statement 3 is incorrect: a thermal decomposition absorbs heat and is endothermic, so it does not give out an enormous amount of heat. The incorrect statements are 1 and 3. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Redox: Oxidation, Reduction and Reducing Agents
stem:
Which of the following statements about the given reaction are correct? \(3\text{Fe(s)} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O(g)} \rightarrow \text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4\text{(s)} + 4\text{H}_2\text{(g)}\)

1. Iron metal is getting oxidised.
2. Water is getting reduced.
3. Water is acting as a reducing agent.
4. Water is acting as an oxidizing agent.
solution: Iron goes from the free element to \(\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4\), gaining oxygen, so iron is oxidised and statement 1 is correct. Hydrogen goes from \(+1\) in water to \(0\) in \(\text{H}_2\), a gain of electrons, so water is reduced and statement 2 is correct. The species that is itself reduced is the oxidising agent, so water is the oxidising agent (statement 4 correct) and not the reducing agent (statement 3 wrong). Hence 1, 2 and 4 hold. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Types of Reactions: Combination, Decomposition, Displacement
stem:
Which among the following is(are) double displacement reaction(s)?

i. \(\text{Pb} + \text{CuCl}_2 \rightarrow \text{PbCl}_2 + \text{Cu}\)
ii. \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{BaCl}_2 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4 + 2\text{NaCl}\)
iii. \(\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\)
iv. \(\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\)
solution: (i) Lead displaces copper from its salt, so it is a single displacement reaction. (ii) Two compounds exchange their ions to give a precipitate of \(\text{BaSO}_4\), which is the defining pattern of a double displacement (precipitation) reaction. (iii) \(\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\) is a combination reaction. (iv) \(\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\) is combustion. Only (ii) is a double displacement. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Stoichiometry and Laws of Chemical Combination
stem: Which one among the following equations is correctly balanced?
solution: Balancing \(\text{NaOH} + \text{Al} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{NaAlO}_2 + \text{H}_2\) gives \(2\text{NaOH} + 2\text{Al} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaAlO}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\). Atom check for option b: Na 2 and 2, Al 2 and 2, O \(2 + 2 = 4\) and \(2 \times 2 = 4\), H \(2 + 4 = 6\) and \(3 \times 2 = 6\). Option a has 1 Na and 1 Al on the left against 4 H on the right, option c puts 8 hydrogen atoms on the right against 6 on the left, and option d has 4 hydrogen atoms on the left against 2 on the right. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Consider the following statements:

1. Breakdown of glucose into carbon dioxide and water is an endothermic reaction.
2. Formation of water from \(\text{H}_2\) and \(\text{O}_2\) is an example of combination reaction.
3. Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is an exothermic reaction.

How many of the above reactions is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is wrong: the breakdown of glucose into carbon dioxide and water (respiration) releases energy and is exothermic, not endothermic. Statement 2 is correct: \(2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\) has two reactants forming a single product, so it is a combination reaction. Statement 3 is correct: decomposition of vegetable matter into compost gives out heat and is exothermic. So exactly two of the three statements are correct. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Specific Reactions: Precipitation, Electrolysis and Daily Life
stem:
Consider the following statements:

1. Quick lime is used for white washing walls.
2. Calcium hydroxide reacts slowly with the carbon dioxide in air to form a thin layer of calcium carbonate on the walls.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: quick lime \(\text{CaO}\) is first slaked, \(\text{CaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\), and it is the solution of slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) that is applied to the walls, not quick lime itself. Statement 2 is correct: \(\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\) proceeds slowly with atmospheric carbon dioxide over two to three days and leaves a shiny thin film of calcium carbonate, which is what gives the whitewashed finish. Only statement 2 is correct. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Consider the following reaction: \(n\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow m\text{PbO} + o\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2\)

The value of \(n\), \(m\) and \(o\) in a balanced equation:
solution: The balanced thermal decomposition of lead nitrate is \(2\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{PbO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2\). Atom check: Pb 2 and 2, N 4 and 4, O on the left \(2 \times 6 = 12\) and on the right \(2 + 8 + 2 = 12\). Hence \(n = 2\), \(m = 2\) and \(o = 4\). Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Consider the following statements:

1. The decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine is an endothermic reaction.
2. The reaction of barium hydroxide and ammonium chloride is an endothermic reaction.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: \(2\text{AgCl} \rightarrow 2\text{Ag} + \text{Cl}_2\) proceeds only when light energy is absorbed, so this photochemical decomposition is endothermic. Statement 2 is correct: barium hydroxide with ammonium chloride is the classic endothermic reaction that absorbs so much heat that the vessel cools below the temperature of its surroundings. Both statements are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Redox: Oxidation, Reduction and Reducing Agents
stem:
Consider the following statements about the oxidation reaction:

1. It involves loss of hydrogen atoms.
2. There is an addition of oxygen atoms.
3. There is a loss of electrons.
4. There is a gain of electrons.
5. The substance loses oxygen.
6. It involves the gain of hydrogen atoms.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Oxidation is defined as addition of oxygen, removal of hydrogen, or loss of electrons. So statements 1 (loss of hydrogen), 2 (addition of oxygen) and 3 (loss of electrons) are correct. Statements 4 (gain of electrons), 5 (loss of oxygen) and 6 (gain of hydrogen) are the three definitions of reduction, not oxidation. Hence 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Types of Reactions: Combination, Decomposition, Displacement
stem:
Consider the following reaction: \(\text{Fe(s)} + \text{CuSO}_4\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{FeSO}_4\text{(aq)} + \text{Cu(s)}\)

1. This is an example of a double displacement reaction.
2. Blue colour of copper sulphate solution fades.
3. Copper has been displaced by iron from its compound.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: a free element replaces one element of a compound, which is a single displacement reaction, not a double displacement (no ion exchange between two compounds). Statement 2 is correct: as \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) is removed from solution and green \(\text{FeSO}_4\) forms, the blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades. Statement 3 is correct: iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate, and the copper deposits as a brown coating on the iron. Hence 2 and 3 are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Redox: Oxidation, Reduction and Reducing Agents
stem: Which one of the following is an oxidation-reduction reaction?
solution: In \(2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO}\), magnesium is oxidised (0 to \(+2\)) and oxygen is reduced (0 to \(-2\)), so it is an oxidation-reduction (redox) reaction. Option a is a neutralisation, option b is a combination with no change in oxidation states, and option d is a double displacement with no change in oxidation states. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Exact duplicate of bank id f62b3174-b7ca-48ec-93b2-b7899cd7da66 (same stem, same four options in the same order). Answer C copied from that row; solution rewritten to strip a corrupted non-ASCII character present in the stored text.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements
1. A warm front occurs when a warm air mass moves over a cold air mass.
2. Since the warm air is lighter, it rises gently over the denser cold air mass.
3. As the warm air rises, it cools adiabatically, leading to condensation and cloud formation.
4. Prolonged and steady precipitation occurs, typically in the form of drizzle or light rain, spread over a small area ahead of the front.

Which of the following statements is / are not correct.
solution: Statement 1 is correct: a warm front is formed where an advancing warm air mass overrides a retreating cold air mass. Statement 2 is correct: the warm air is lighter and less dense, so it glides gently up over the wedge of denser cold air along a very gentle slope. Statement 3 is correct: the ascending warm air expands and cools adiabatically, reaching dew point, which causes condensation and a characteristic sequence of clouds (cirrus, cirrostratus, altostratus, nimbostratus). Statement 4 is NOT correct: because the warm front slope is very gentle, the cloud shield and the resulting prolonged, steady drizzle or light rain extend over a very LARGE area, often several hundred kilometres ahead of the surface front, not a small area. Only statement 4 is incorrect. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding 'fronts':
1. The movement of a front causes a slow change in weather in the area over which it moves.
2. Cold fronts are associated with thunderstorms.
3. Warm front is the boundary between an advancing mass of warm air where it is overriding and rising above a mass of colder air.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: fronts are zones of steep temperature and pressure gradient, and the passage of a front brings an abrupt, not a slow, change of weather. Statement 2 is correct: a cold front has a steep slope, forces the warm air up violently and produces cumulonimbus clouds and thunderstorms. Statement 3 is correct: a warm front is precisely the boundary where an advancing warm air mass overrides and rises above a colder air mass. So the correct combination is '2 and 3 only', which is not among the printed options. Since statement 1 is definitely wrong, every option containing it must be rejected, which leaves only option C. Matches option C.
reviewNote: PRINTED DEFECT: the correct combination '2 and 3 only' is not offered. The identical question exists in the bank as e6de738f with the full option set (A. 1 only / B. 1 and 2 only / C. 2 and 3 only / D. 1, 2 and 3) keyed C = '2 and 3 only'. Here the option set is corrupted; keyed C ('3 only') as the only option that excludes the false statement 1. NOT marked dup because the option set differs materially.

subject: Geography
stem:
Normally, the temperature decreases with the increase in height from the Earth's surface, because
1. the atmosphere can be heated upwards only from the Earth's surface
2. there is more moisture in the upper atmosphere
3. the air is less dense in the upper atmosphere

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
solution: Statement 1 is correct: the atmosphere is largely transparent to incoming short-wave solar radiation and is heated chiefly from below by long-wave terrestrial radiation, so layers nearer the surface are warmer. Statement 2 is incorrect: water vapour is concentrated in the lower troposphere and DECREASES rapidly with height, so there is less, not more, moisture aloft. Statement 3 is correct: the air is thinner and less dense with height, so it contains fewer molecules of the gases and dust that absorb and retain heat. Hence 1 and 3 explain the normal lapse rate. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the tropical zone, the western sections of the oceans are warmer than the eastern sections owing to the influence of trade winds.
2. In the temperate zone, westerlies make the eastern sections of oceans warmer than the western sections.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: the trade winds blow from east to west in the tropics and drive warm water westward, piling it up on the western side of the oceans, while the eastern sides experience cold upwelling and cool currents such as the Peru and Benguela currents. Statement 2 is correct: in temperate latitudes the westerlies drive the warm water eastward, so warm drifts such as the North Atlantic Drift and the North Pacific Drift make the eastern sections warm, whereas the western sections receive cold currents such as the Labrador and Oyashio currents. Both statements are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem:
The annual range of temperature in the interior of the continents is high as compared to coastal areas. What is/are the reason/reasons?
1. Thermal difference between land and water
2. Variation in altitude between continents and oceans
3. Presence of strong winds in the interior
4. Heavy rains in the interior as compared to coasts

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
solution: Statement 1 is the correct reason: this is continentality. Land has a low specific heat and heats and cools rapidly, while water has a high specific heat and heats and cools slowly, so continental interiors have hot summers and cold winters and thus a large annual range, whereas coasts are moderated by the sea. Statement 2 is not a reason: altitude affects the actual temperature of a place, not the land-sea contrast that produces the annual range, and there is no systematic altitude rule of this kind. Statement 3 is wrong: interiors are not characterised by strong winds, and in any case wind would moderate rather than widen the range. Statement 4 is factually wrong: interiors generally get LESS rain than coasts. Only reason 1 holds. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: What is the effect of Chinook winds in the central plains in the USA?
solution: The Chinook is a hot, dry local wind that descends the eastern (leeward) slopes of the Rockies and warms adiabatically as it sinks. Blowing in winter over the prairies of the USA and Canada, it raises the temperature sharply in a short time and melts the snow cover, which is why it is called the 'snow-eater' and is valued by ranchers for keeping pastures open for cattle. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem:
Assertion (A): Thickness of the atmosphere is maximum over the Equator.
Reason (R): High insolation and strong convection currents occur over the Equator.
optA: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A.
optB: Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
optC: A is true but R is false.
optD: A is false but R is true.
solution: The assertion is true: the atmosphere, and in particular the troposphere, is thickest over the equator, where it extends to about 16 to 18 km, against only about 8 km over the poles. The reason is also true: the equator receives the highest insolation because the sun's rays are nearly vertical there, which sets up strong thermal convection currents. Those rising convection currents push the top of the troposphere and the tropopause upward, so the strong heating and convection is precisely the cause of the greater thickness. R correctly explains A. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The annual range of temperature is greater in the Pacific Ocean than that in the Atlantic Ocean.
2. The annual range of temperature is greater in the Northern Hemisphere than that in the Southern Hemisphere.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: the annual range of surface temperature is greater in the Atlantic Ocean than in the Pacific Ocean, because the Atlantic is narrower and is enclosed by large landmasses on both sides, so it feels the continental influence strongly, whereas the vast Pacific is dominated by a maritime regime and has a smaller range. Statement 2 is correct: the Northern Hemisphere has a far greater proportion of land, and land heats and cools faster than water, so the annual range of temperature there is much greater than in the water-dominated Southern Hemisphere. Only statement 2 is correct. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following phenomena happens in India when the Sun shines vertically over the Tropic of Capricorn?
optA: High pressure develops over North-West India
optB: Low pressure develops over North-West India
optC: No change in pressure occurs over North-West India
solution: The sun is vertically overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn around 22 December, the winter solstice, which is mid-winter in India. With low insolation the land cools rapidly, the air becomes cold and dense and subsides, so a strong high-pressure cell develops over North-West India and adjoining Central Asia. It is from this winter high that the dry north-east monsoon, or the retreating land winds, blow outwards towards the sea. Options B and D describe the summer situation, when the sun is over the Tropic of Cancer and a thermal low forms over North-West India. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Both the belts over the oceans at about \(30^\circ\) to \(35^\circ\) NORTH and SOUTH Latitudes are known as Horse latitude.
2. Horse latitudes are low pressure belts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: the calm belts lying over the oceans at about \(30^\circ\) to \(35^\circ\) north and south of the equator are called the Horse latitudes, the name coming from sailing days when becalmed ships threw horses overboard for want of water. Statement 2 is incorrect: these are the subtropical HIGH pressure belts, produced by the descent of air of the Hadley circulation, and the sinking air makes them calm, dry and the source region of both the trade winds and the westerlies. Only statement 1 is correct. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to structure of the earth's atmosphere:
1. Thickness of the troposphere is greatest at the equator.
2. The air temperature of the tropopause is a bit higher at the poles than at the equator.
3. The temperature in troposphere decreases at the rate of 1 degree F for every 165 m of height

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
solution: Troposphere is thickest at equator (1 correct). Tropopause temperature is least cold (highest) over poles (2 correct). Statement 3 is not accurate for the standard lapse rate. Matches option B: 1 and 2 only.
reviewNote: DUP of bank id f599d030 (same three statements, same option set); answer B and solution copied from that row. Bank also carries a near-identical twin 77c5e8fb, likewise keyed B.

subject: Geography
stem: In the South Atlantic and SouthEastern Pacific regions in tropical latitudes, cyclones do not originate. What is the reason?
optD: Absence of land in those regions
solution: Tropical cyclones need a pre-existing zone of low-level convergence and disturbance to organise around, which the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone normally supplies. Over the South Atlantic and the south-eastern Pacific the ITCZ stays well north of the equator and seldom shifts into these waters, so the required seed disturbance is missing. These regions are further handicapped by cold currents (Benguela and Humboldt) that keep sea surface temperatures below the roughly \(27^\circ\)C threshold and by strong vertical wind shear. Option A is false as stated, sea surface temperatures there are low, not high. Option C is wrong because the Coriolis force is weak only within a few degrees of the equator, not throughout these regions. Option D is irrelevant, since cyclones form over the ocean. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Option (a) is printed as 'Sea surface temperatures are high'; the standard version of this question prints 'Sea surface temperatures are low'. Either way the key (b) is unaffected, so not marked flawed.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. In mountainous regions, during the day, air moves upslope, and the air from the valley blows up the valley, which is known as the mountain breeze.
2. The cool air of the high plateaus and ice fields draining into the valley is called katabatic wind.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect only in its name: the daytime wind that moves up the slopes and up the valley is the VALLEY breeze, not the mountain breeze. The mountain breeze is the opposite, the night-time flow of cooled, dense air down the slopes into the valley. Statement 2 is correct: the very cold, heavy air of high plateaus and ice fields that drains down into the valleys under gravity is the katabatic wind, which is a stronger and larger-scale version of the same downslope drainage. Only statement 2 is correct. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Weather refers to the sum total of weather conditions and variations over a large area for a long period of time.
2. Climate refers to the state of the atmosphere over an area at any point of time.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: The two definitions have been interchanged. Statement 1 is incorrect: the sum total of weather conditions and variations over a large area for a long period of time, conventionally about thirty years, is CLIMATE, not weather. Statement 2 is incorrect: the momentary state of the atmosphere over an area at any given point of time is WEATHER, not climate. Since both definitions are swapped, neither statement is correct. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements about the Heat Zones of the Earth.
1. The Torrid Zone is the area which receives the maximum heat.
2. The temperate zone is the area bounded by the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle in the Northern Hemisphere.
3. In Frigid Zones, the Sunrise is much above the horizon.

Which of the statements given above is/are not correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: the Torrid Zone, lying between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, receives the vertical rays of the mid-day sun at some time of the year and therefore gets the maximum heat. Statement 2 is correct: the North Temperate Zone is exactly the belt bounded by the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle in the Northern Hemisphere, and it has moderate temperatures because the sun is never overhead there. Statement 3 is NOT correct: in the Frigid Zones, which lie beyond the Arctic and Antarctic Circles, the sun does NOT rise much above the horizon, so its rays are always very slanting and give very little heat. Only statement 3 is incorrect. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem:
Which of the following statements related to the 'trade winds' is/are correct?
1. These are permanent winds flowing from east to west.
2. These are warm winds, and hence they bring heavy rainfall to the western sides of the tropical islands.
3. The eastern parts of the trade winds associated with the cool ocean currents are drier and more stable than the western parts of the ocean.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
solution: Statement 1 is correct: the trades are permanent or planetary winds blowing from the subtropical high pressure belts towards the equatorial low, and after Coriolis deflection they blow as the north-east and south-east trades, that is, broadly from east to west. Statement 2 is incorrect: because the trades approach from the east, they strike the EASTERN, windward sides of tropical islands and it is those coasts that get heavy orographic rainfall, while the western, leeward sides lie in a rain shadow. Statement 3 is correct: the eastern parts of the tropical oceans, next to the west coasts of the continents, are washed by cool currents such as the Canary, Benguela and Peru currents, which chill the lower air, create stable conditions and suppress convection, making these margins dry, which is why the coastal deserts occur there. So statements 1 and 3 are correct. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the Earth's heat budget:
1. The Earth maintains a near balance between incoming solar radiation and outgoing terrestrial radiation.
2. Clouds increase the amount of shortwave radiation absorbed by the Earth's surface.
3. Greenhouse gases primarily absorb longwave radiation emitted by the Earth.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: this near equality of incoming insolation and outgoing terrestrial radiation is precisely what is meant by the heat budget, and it is why the mean temperature of the Earth stays nearly constant over long periods. Statement 2 is incorrect: clouds have a high albedo and reflect a large share of incoming shortwave radiation straight back to space, so they REDUCE, not increase, the shortwave radiation absorbed at the surface. Statement 3 is correct: the atmosphere is largely transparent to incoming shortwave radiation, whereas greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, water vapour and methane strongly absorb the longwave, infra-red radiation emitted by the Earth and re-radiate part of it downwards. Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following is the primary factor that determines the type of precipitation that falls to the ground?
optA: The temperature at the cloud level.
optB: The wind speed at the cloud level.
optC: The humidity level at the ground level.
solution: Whether precipitation reaches the ground as rain, snow, sleet or hail is decided by temperature. If the temperature in the cloud and in the air below stays above freezing the droplets fall as rain; if it is below freezing the water vapour condenses directly into ice crystals and falls as snow; partial melting followed by refreezing gives sleet, and repeated vertical circulation in a freezing cumulonimbus gives hail. Wind speed and cloud altitude at most influence the size or intensity of the fall, and ground humidity affects evaporation of the falling drops, but none of them decides the FORM. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Strictly the form of precipitation is set by the temperature profile of the whole air column between cloud and ground, not by the cloud-level temperature alone; option (a) is nevertheless the only temperature-based option and is clearly the intended key.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding fronts?
optA: The higher the temperature difference between two air masses the lower the thickness of the front formed between them.
optB: Fronts are the typical features of mid-latitudes.
optC: The weather along a cold front is violent with drop in temperature and heavy showers.
optD: A warm front moves up to twice as quickly as a cold front.
solution: Option A is a correct statement: the greater the temperature contrast between the two air masses, the sharper and steeper the frontal surface, so the transition zone between them is thinner. Option B is correct: fronts form where contrasting tropical and polar air masses meet, which is characteristically in the mid-latitudes, and they are absent in the tropics. Option C is correct: a cold front has a steep slope and forces the warm air up abruptly, so its weather is violent, with cumulonimbus cloud, heavy showers, squalls and a sharp fall of temperature after its passage. Option D is NOT correct, and it is stated backwards: it is the COLD front that advances roughly twice as fast as the warm front, which is exactly why a fast cold front eventually overtakes the warm front and produces an occlusion. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth in Space, Maps and Coordinates
stem:
Arrange the following zones in ascending order in terms of their latitudinal extent on the Earth surface :
1. Equatorial zone
2. Midlatitude zone
3. Subarctic zone
4. Tropical zone

Select the answer using the code given below :
solution: Extents: Equatorial (~0-5) < Tropical (0-23.5) < Midlatitude (35-60) < Subarctic (60-70). Ascending order: 1-4-2-3. Matches option C.
